the output value. In order to do that, the function find_memberships has
been changed to return also the new upsampled universe. Hence, the functions
which uses find_memberships (only once in visualization) has been adapted to its new call.

Many modificaions to PhysicalDevice and subclasses to manage instantiation

Many aspects of instantiations are general: idProduct, idVendor must match and can be validated before initialize().  The communication channel is only opened in doInitializeDevice(): a PhysicalDevice can be created even if it is not connected, the initializeDevice will simply fail.

To allow DeviceManager() to instantiate any class, they must have a __init__ that is standard.  Hence, all __init__ have been modified to include these three named parameters.

Also, for historical reasons, productId, and vendorId have been changed to idProduct and idVendor.

Finally, the DeviceManager(), upon recognizing that a device was connected, will attempt to match a subclass of PhysicalDevice: this is a two-step process: 1) __init__ (which can raise an incompatible class exception and 2) initialize that will attempt to communicate with the device.  Devices cannot be initialized automatically because they will lock the communication channel for all  instances, preventing any communications even for USB diagnostic purposes.

On the flake8 test selection, this PR does _not_ focus on "_style violations_" (the majority of flake8 error codes that [__psf/black__](https://github.com/psf/black) can autocorrect).  Instead these tests are focus on runtime safety and correctness:
* E9 tests are about Python syntax errors usually raised because flake8 can not build an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).  Often these issues are a sign of unused code or code that has not been ported to Python 3.  These would be compile-time errors in a compiled language but in a dynamic language like Python they result in the script halting/crashing on the user.
* F63 tests are usually about the confusion between identity and equality in Python.  Use ==/!= to compare str, bytes, and int literals is the classic case.  These are areas where __a == b__ is True but __a is b__ is False (or vice versa).  Python >= 3.8 will raise SyntaxWarnings on these instances.
* F7 tests logic errors and syntax errors in type hints
* F82 tests are almost always _undefined names_ which are usually a sign of a typo, missing imports, or code that has not been ported to Python 3.  These also would be compile-time errors in a compiled language but in Python a __NameError__ is raised which will halt/crash the script on the user.

This function interpolates the x values from the domain of the fuzzy variable
such that their membership function values are the parameter y (`u(xx)==y`)

This function is used to upsample the universe definition when defuzzify
the output value. In order to do that, the function find_memberships has
been changed to return also the new upsampled universe. Hence, the functions
which uses find_memberships (only once in visualization) has been adapted to its new call.
Finally, the imports and __all__ usage has been adapted including the new function.

Many modificaions to PhysicalDevice and subclasses to manage instantiation

Many aspects of instantiations are general: idProduct, idVendor must match and can be validated before initialize().  The communication channel is only opened in doInitializeDevice(): a PhysicalDevice can be created even if it is not connected, the initializeDevice will simply fail.

To allow DeviceManager() to instantiate any class, they must have a __init__ that is standard.  Hence, all __init__ have been modified to include these three named parameters.

Also, for historical reasons, productId, and vendorId have been changed to idProduct and idVendor.

Finally, the DeviceManager(), upon recognizing that a device was connected, will attempt to match a subclass of PhysicalDevice: this is a two-step process: 1) __init__ (which can raise an incompatible class exception and 2) initialize that will attempt to communicate with the device.  Devices cannot be initialized automatically because they will lock the communication channel for all  instances, preventing any communications even for USB diagnostic purposes.

On the flake8 test selection, this PR does _not_ focus on "_style violations_" (the majority of flake8 error codes that [__psf/black__](https://github.com/psf/black) can autocorrect).  Instead these tests are focus on runtime safety and correctness:
* E9 tests are about Python syntax errors usually raised because flake8 can not build an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).  Often these issues are a sign of unused code or code that has not been ported to Python 3.  These would be compile-time errors in a compiled language but in a dynamic language like Python they result in the script halting/crashing on the user.
* F63 tests are usually about the confusion between identity and equality in Python.  Use ==/!= to compare str, bytes, and int literals is the classic case.  These are areas where __a == b__ is True but __a is b__ is False (or vice versa).  Python >= 3.8 will raise SyntaxWarnings on these instances.
* F7 tests logic errors and syntax errors in type hints
* F82 tests are almost always _undefined names_ which are usually a sign of a typo, missing imports, or code that has not been ported to Python 3.  These also would be compile-time errors in a compiled language but in Python a __NameError__ is raised which will halt/crash the script on the user.

TSK consequents are used as Fuzzy terms. The difference is that in TSK
terms the mf attribute is a Polynomial object, which contains the domain
and the expression (polynomial), which is a string using the same names of the
input variables.

other issues).

The function interp_value has been implemented.
This function interpolates the x values from the domain of the fuzzy variable
such that their membership function values are the parameter y (`u(xx)==y`)

This function is used to upsample the universe definition when defuzzify
the output value. In order to do that, the function find_memberships has
been changed to return also the new upsampled universe. Hence, the functions
which uses find_memberships (only once in visualization) has been adapted to its new call.
Finally, the imports and __all__ usage has been adapted including the new function.

Many modificaions to PhysicalDevice and subclasses to manage instantiation

Many aspects of instantiations are general: idProduct, idVendor must match and can be validated before initialize().  The communication channel is only opened in doInitializeDevice(): a PhysicalDevice can be created even if it is not connected, the initializeDevice will simply fail.

To allow DeviceManager() to instantiate any class, they must have a __init__ that is standard.  Hence, all __init__ have been modified to include these three named parameters.

Also, for historical reasons, productId, and vendorId have been changed to idProduct and idVendor.

Finally, the DeviceManager(), upon recognizing that a device was connected, will attempt to match a subclass of PhysicalDevice: this is a two-step process: 1) __init__ (which can raise an incompatible class exception and 2) initialize that will attempt to communicate with the device.  Devices cannot be initialized automatically because they will lock the communication channel for all  instances, preventing any communications even for USB diagnostic purposes.

On the flake8 test selection, this PR does _not_ focus on "_style violations_" (the majority of flake8 error codes that [__psf/black__](https://github.com/psf/black) can autocorrect).  Instead these tests are focus on runtime safety and correctness:
* E9 tests are about Python syntax errors usually raised because flake8 can not build an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).  Often these issues are a sign of unused code or code that has not been ported to Python 3.  These would be compile-time errors in a compiled language but in a dynamic language like Python they result in the script halting/crashing on the user.
* F63 tests are usually about the confusion between identity and equality in Python.  Use ==/!= to compare str, bytes, and int literals is the classic case. Many modificaions to PhysicalDevice and subclasses to manage instantiation

Many aspects of instantiations are general: idProduct, idVendor must match and can be validated before initialize().  The communication channel is only opened in doInitializeDevice(): a PhysicalDevice can be created even if it is not connected, the initializeDevice will simply fail.

To allow DeviceManager() to instantiate any class, they must have a __init__ that is standard.  Hence, all __init__ have been modified to include these three named parameters.

Also, for historical reasons, productId, and vendorId have been changed to idProduct and idVendor.

Finally, the DeviceManager(), upon recognizing that a device was connected, will attempt to match a subclass of PhysicalDevice: this is a two-step process: 1) __init__ (which can raise an incompatible class exception and 2) initialize that will attempt to communicate with the device.  Devices cannot be initialized automatically because they will lock the communication channel for all  instances, preventing any communications even for USB diagnostic purposes.

https://flake8.pycqa.org/en/latest/user/error-codes.html

On the flake8 test selection, this PR does _not_ focus on "_style violations_" (the majority of flake8 error codes that [__psf/black__](https://github.com/psf/black) can autocorrect).  Instead these tests are focus on runtime safety and correctness:
* E9 tests are about Python syntax errors usually raised because flake8 can not build an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).  Often these issues are a sign of unused code or code that has not been ported to Python 3.  These would be compile-time errors in a compiled language but in a dynamic language like Python they result in the script halting/crashing on the user.
* F63 tests are usually about the confusion between identity and equality in Python.  Use ==/!= to compare str, bytes, and int literals is the classic case.  These are areas where __a == b__ is True but __a is b__ is False (or vice versa).  Python >= 3.8 will raise SyntaxWarnings on these instances.
* F7 tests logic errors and syntax errors in type hints
* F82 tests are almost always _undefined names_ which are usually a sign of a typo, missing imports, or code that has not been ported to Python 3.  These also would be compile-time errors in a compiled language but in Python a __NameError__ is raised which will halt/crash the script on the user.
